item.title: #3586147: Accessibility tools -- switch to Editoria11y 3.x
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +91/−22 · yml +87/−21 · json +4/−1
  • Diff: fc7531c
  • Discussion: #3586147 · 3 contributors · 15 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

The Drupal CMS accessibility tools recipe now depends on Editoria11y 3.x instead of 2.x. The issue says 2.x is functionally end-of-life. According to the issue, 3.x ships with 16 languages (2.x only had German), has more tests, rewritten tips, CSV exports moved to a submodule, and dashboard views that can filter on live node data. The Editoria11y results dashboard view that the recipe ships was rewritten to match the new 3.x data model.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: The accessibility tools recipe now requires drupal/editoria11y ^3 instead of ^2.2.
  • Config change: The A11y Tools Editoria11y results view now uses the Editoria11y 3.x tables ed11y_result and ed11y_page, with page_result_count replaced by content_results.

Technical details

The recipe's composer.json requirement changes from drupal/editoria11y: ^2.2 to ^3. The root composer.json also adds an exclusion for modules/editoria11y_export/tests under drupal/editoria11y, next to the other per-package test exclusions.

The recipe's A11y Tools Editoria11y results view config was updated for the 3.x schema. The base table changes from editoria11y_results to ed11y_result. A new relationship editoria11y_result_to_page joins to ed11y_page, and the page_title, page_path and result count fields now come from ed11y_page through it. The page_result_count field and sort become content_results, and a hidden pid field is added. The editoria11y_sync_check header now uses table views.

The view only works with Editoria11y 3.x tables, so it will not work with 2.x.

item.title: #3591532: Drupal CMS installer denies access after site template selection on Drupal core 11.4.13
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +13/−0 · php +13
  • Diff: d6c5d89
  • Discussion: #3591532 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

The Drupal CMS web installer showed 'Access denied: The installation can only be continued in the browser session that started it' after choosing a site template and clicking Next on Drupal core 11.4.13. This came from the session check core added in SA-CORE-2026-017. The Drupal CMS installer profile now works around it, so fresh installs on patched core complete normally.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Core stores an install_session_token in the session so only one browser can continue the installer. In drupal_cms_installer_install_profile(), the token had not yet been saved when modules were installed. The module install rebuilds the container, which discards unsaved session data and gives the request a new session object. The fix reads the token via Drupal::request()->getSession()->get('install_session_token') before ModuleInstallerInterface::install(). After install_install_profile() it sets the token back on the fresh session object, if one was present. The change is in the Drupal CMS installer profile code. The code comments point to install_bootstrap_full() and DrupalKernel::initializeContainer().

item.title: #3591533: setComponentTree fails when a second module with components is installed in the same recipe run
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +2/−6 · php +2/−6
  • Diff: f99cbf8
  • Discussion: #3591533 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Applying a recipe that installs two or more modules providing components, where each module's recipe uses the setComponentTree config action, no longer fails for the second module. Previously this crashed with an AssertionError, though applying the same recipes in separate runs worked.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

SetComponentTree::setComponentVersions() guarded generateComponents() with a static $generated flag, so Canvas components were generated only once per request. Components from a module installed later in the same recipe run did not exist when its tree was processed, and the assert($component instanceof ComponentInterface) check failed. The issue proposed regenerating only when a component is missing. The merged change instead removes the static flag, so componentSourceManager->generateComponents() runs on every call to setComponentVersions(). The fix is in the drupal_cms_helper module.

item.title: #3591524: Search is 404 for non top-level pages
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +18/−1 · php +17 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: bbf033e
  • Discussion: #3591524 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

The search form in Drupal CMS's search feature submitted to a relative search URL. From any page below the top level, such as /recipes/borscht-with-pork-ribs, it went to /recipes/search, which is a 404. The form now submits to the correct search page from any page, including on sites with language prefixes or installed in a subdirectory.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The search view had been changed from a page display to a block display (#3591455), with link_display: custom_url and link_url: search. A block display has no route, so ViewExecutable::hasUrl() returns FALSE and ViewsExposedForm::buildForm() falls back to getPath() on the display handler. That returns the link_url value unchanged, so it becomes the form action without a base path or language prefix.

The shipped fix changes the view config to link_url: /search. It also adds a form_views_exposed_form_alter hook, FormHooks::alterViewsExposedForm(), which rewrites a #action that starts with / using Url::fromUri('base:' . $form['#action'])->toString(). This adds the base path and language handling that Views skips. It is a workaround, marked with a @todo to remove it once the upstream fix in https://www.drupal.org/i/3638040 is released. ComponentValidationTest now enables drupal_cms_helper so the test environment includes the polyfill.

item.title: #3591527: 🤖 drupal_cms_site_template_base leaves two Navigation components enabled in Canvas
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +15/−1 · php +14 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: 6db154b
  • Discussion: #3591527 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

On fresh Drupal CMS installs using the Blank or Starter template, two Navigation module components (navigation.title and navigation.message) stayed enabled and appeared in the Canvas component library, even though they are only meant for the administrative UI. The base site template now disables both. Only new installs are affected; existing sites keep both components enabled.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Recipe action ?canvas.component.sdc.navigation.title replaced by wildcard canvas.component.sdc.navigation.* in drupal_cms_site_template_base.

Technical details

The base recipe had ?canvas.component.sdc.navigation.title, but the component doesn't exist when the recipe's config action runs, so the ? made it skip. Canvas creates the SDC components later, during content import (RecipeSubscriber::ensureComponentsExist()), enabled by default. navigation.message had no line at all. Per the issue, Canvas re-runs the recipe's component actions after apply (RecipeSubscriber::onApply()) but only for names starting with canvas.component., so the ? line was never re-run, and removing the ? alone failed the install because the entity did not exist.

The fix replaces the line in the recipe's config actions with the wildcard canvas.component.sdc.navigation.* with disable: []. A wildcard may match nothing on the first pass, and Canvas's re-run then disables both components once they exist. BasicFunctionalityTest now loads all sdc components with provider navigation and asserts each is disabled.

Upgrade

Existing sites are not changed. To hide the components on an existing site, disable canvas.component.sdc.navigation.title and canvas.component.sdc.navigation.message in the Canvas component settings.

item.title: #3591521: Remove the hardcoded LLM configuration since it will not work with Amazee
item.description:

  • Changes: 1 file, +1/−6 · yml +1/−6
  • Diff: 0cb3fad

Summary

The default Drupal CMS AI assistant no longer ships with preset model parameters (token limit, temperature and similar). These values worked with OpenAI and Anthropic models but would break when Amazee is the provider. The assistant now starts with an empty configuration, so the chosen provider's own defaults apply.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Default llm_configuration in the drupal_cms_assistant AI assistant config is now an empty object instead of hardcoded max_tokens, temperature, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty and top_p values.

In the ai_assistant_api.ai_assistant.drupal_cms_assistant config, llm_configuration was changed from max_tokens: 4096, temperature: 1.0, frequency_penalty: 0, presence_penalty: 0 and top_p: 1.0 to an empty mapping ({ }). llm_provider: __default__ and llm_model: '' are unchanged, so the provider and model still come from the site's default AI provider settings. The motivation was a bug in the AI module's assistant system (ai work item 3586815, MR 2106), which would expose the incompatibility with Amazee once merged. The diff only touches this one default config file. The diff output does not show the file path, so the path comes from the issue text.

Existing sites keep their stored config. Only new installs get the empty default. Sites that hit the Amazee problem can clear the same keys in the assistant's configuration:

item.title: #3591507: Add a hard opt-out for telemetry via settings.php
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591507 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS now has a hard telemetry opt-out in settings.php. Setting $settings['drupal_cms_telemetry'] = FALSE; turns usage data sharing off for every environment that uses that file. The setting overrides the state value, the Site information checkbox, Drush and the install-time DRUPAL_CMS_TELEMETRY environment variable, so an admin can no longer turn it back on. The Site information checkbox is shown disabled and unchecked, with a note that telemetry has been disabled in settings.php. Without the setting, behaviour is unchanged.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New optional $settings['drupal_cms_telemetry'] in settings.php; when FALSE, telemetry is always off.

Technical details

The drupal_cms_helper module's TelemetryManager gets a KILL_SWITCH constant (same value as QUEUE_NAME, drupal_cms_telemetry) and a static isDisabled() method, which returns TRUE only when Settings::get() for that key is strictly FALSE. TelemetryManager::status() checks it first and returns FALSE before reading or writing state, so a call like status(TRUE) cannot re-enable telemetry. Other code that asks status() whether telemetry is on sees FALSE.

In TelemetryHooks, the Site information form alter marks the telemetry checkbox #disabled and replaces the description with "Telemetry has been disabled in settings.php." The usual description and the saveTelemetrySetting submit handler are only added when the kill switch is not set. The user guide page docs/src/updates/telemetry.md documents the setting. Tests: a kernel test, testSettingsKillSwitch, and a functional check in TelemetryOptOutTest that the checkbox is disabled.

The diff has no code that explicitly clears an existing queue when the setting is present, so the issue's "clear the queue" item is not verified here. The issue's open question about showing this on the Status report was not addressed in the diff.

Upgrade

To opt out across all environments, add this to settings.php:

$settings['drupal_cms_telemetry'] = FALSE;

item.title: #3591501: Add an event or param to track use of the launcher
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed

Summary

Drupal CMS's weekly telemetry ping now includes a launcher true/false value. It tells the project team which sites run through the Drupal CMS launcher app. It is sent only when telemetry is enabled. item.title: #3591510: Switch `drush si` default site template to Forma
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591510 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

When Drupal CMS is installed non-interactively with drush si and no site template is named, the default is now Forma instead of Starter. The issue frames this as a test of 1-2 weeks. Starter is the most popular template in analytics, and the maintainers want to know whether that is only because it was the default. I could not read the merged diff, so this describes the prior code and the issue text only. The interactive installer's default (Blank) is not part of the issue.

item.title: #3591506: Updates to telemetry for env info, remove user_login, specify recipes & templates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591506 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS telemetry changed in what it reports. Every event now carries an environment label (ddev, local, dev, staging, production, or ?) in place of the old production flag. The weekly ping also says whether the site appears to run under the Drupal CMS launcher app. The user_login event, which sent a hashed user ID, is gone. Recipe and site template names are now sent only if they are on a fixed allowlist. Anything else is reported as ?. Installs from the command line also record whether the site template was named explicitly. A new DRUPAL_CMS_TELEMETRY environment variable (0 or 1) is applied when the helper module is installed. The telemetry documentation was updated to match.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New DRUPAL_CMS_TELEMETRY environment variable (0 or 1) sets the telemetry status when drupal_cms_helper is installed. Telemetry is still stored per environment.

Technical details

TelemetryManager::log() now sets an environment property, replacing is_production. It comes from the drupal-environment library, and only when Environment is autoloadable. Local environments report ddev or local. Otherwise the order is dev, staging, production, then ?.

TelemetryHooks drops the user_login hook and the Telemetry::Login case. The weekly ping adds a launcher boolean. It is true when the root composer.json extra has a drupal-launcher key and PHP_SAPI === 'cli-server'. ProjectResolver::readPackageInfo() now returns mixed so it can read extra. The code component insert hook now skips events during install and config sync.

RecipeSubscriber::onApply() no longer reads the recipe's Custom type or the extra.drupal_cms.no_telemetry flag. Both are replaced by isReportable(), which matches the recipe directory name against the new Telemetry::SITE_TEMPLATES, CONTRIB_RECIPES and CORE_RECIPES constants (a trailing * is a prefix match). Names that don't match are sent as ?. Recipes applied while installing from a site template are no longer logged. For Site recipes during install, the event includes cli. When run from the CLI, it also includes cli_specified, true if the recipe path appears in argv. Telemetry::CUSTOM_EXTENSION is renamed CUSTOM_MODULE, since only modules can now be custom. The DRUPAL_CMS_TELEMETRY handling moved from the recipe subscriber into drupal_cms_helper_install(). The recipe analysis output code was also reorganised. The project template composer.json now runs post-update-cmd on post-install-cmd too.

Summary

item.title: #3591505: Update ping to weekly and add increment property
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591505 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS's telemetry "still alive" ping is now sent every 7 days instead of every 30. Each ping includes a count of how many pings the site has sent, so the Drupal CMS team can tell how long a site has existed. This lets them separate short-lived test, prototype and demo sites from long-running ones. The telemetry documentation page is updated to describe the new interval and the counter.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The change is in TelemetryHooks::cron() in drupal_cms_helper. PING_INTERVAL goes from 86400 * 30 to 86400 * 7. The drupal_cms_telemetry.ping state value used to hold the last ping timestamp. It now holds a two-item array of [last ping timestamp, ping count]. A legacy numeric value is converted to [$last, 0] on read, so existing sites carry on without an update hook.

Each ping carries count, which is the stored count plus one. The first ping (count of 1) still adds opt_in and, for drupal/cms or drupal/cms_cpanel root packages, project_name. The state is only written back when a ping is actually logged. The old if ($this->telemetry->status()) wrapper around the ping logic is removed. Now only sendAll() is guarded by the status check, and TelemetryManager::sendAll() gains an assert($this->status()). TelemetryManager::log() still checks status() itself, so no ping event is queued while telemetry is disabled. The state is still updated in that case, so the counter advances even when no event is recorded.

TelemetryHooksTest now asserts count of 1 and then 2. docs/src/updates/telemetry.md is updated. In the diff the edited table row ends with an extra ||.

item.title: #3591455: Update search recipe to create blocks instead of a views page
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591455 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The Drupal CMS search recipe no longer creates a /search page for results. It now provides a views block for the results, which can be placed on a Canvas page. The issue author found the page-based setup unintuitive and noted that it had been a rushed change before the 2.0 launch. With the recipe applied, site builders create their own Canvas page and add the search form and results components to it.

In recipes/drupal_cms_search/config/views.view.search.yml, the page display is replaced by a display with id search, titled "Block", using the block plugin. The path: search setting is removed and exposed_block: true is kept. This produces two Canvas components, block.views_block.search-search for the results and block.views_exposed_filter_block.search-search for the exposed form. They replace the single block.views_exposed_filter_block.search-page component.

item.title: #3591502: Installer writes Composer's cache into <project root>/.composer when installing a site template
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591502 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

When COMPOSER_HOME isn't set, the Drupal CMS installer falls back to a .composer directory in the project root so Composer can run. That fallback also caused Composer's download cache to be written to .composer/cache/, leaving hundreds of changed files in version-controlled or repository-deployed code directories after installing a site template. The installer now disables Composer's cache in that situation, so the project stays clean. This affected 2.2.3 through 2.2.5.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In ComposerExecutor::execute() (drupal_cms_installer/src/ComposerExecutor.php), when the COMPOSER_HOME fallback is applied, the installer now also sets COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR to /dev/null (NUL on Windows) via Platform::putEnv(), and clears it in the finally cleanup along with COMPOSER_HOME and COMPOSER_HTACCESS_PROTECT. Composer's Factory::getCacheDir() otherwise derives the cache path from COMPOSER_HOME, which is why the cache landed in the project. A null cache dir makes Composer disable its cache, so no cache directory is created. This was chosen over the two options in the issue: passing --no-cache in run(), and a per-project temp directory. Because it is only applied when the fallback is used, sites with a real COMPOSER_HOME keep their normal cache. The unit test ComposerExecutorTest now asserts COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR is set inside execute() and unset afterwards, and that a real ComposerExecutor::run() doesn't create the .composer directory.

Upgrade

If a site already ran the installer on 2.2.3 to 2.2.5 without COMPOSER_HOME set, an existing <project root>/.composer/cache/ directory may remain and can be deleted or excluded from version control.

item.title: #3591504: Telemetry checkbox prevents Basic site settings from being saved
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591504 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In Drupal CMS, the telemetry opt-in checkbox added to the Basic site settings form (/admin/config/system/site-information) broke saving of that form. Changes to the site name, slogan, email, front page and 403/404 pages were discarded, the page reloaded with the old values, and no confirmation message appeared. Only the telemetry checkbox was stored. The fix makes the form save normally again, together with the telemetry setting. The issue reports it on drupal_cms_helper 2.2.5.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In drupal_cms_helper/src/Hook/TelemetryHooks.php, alterSiteInformationForm() attached saveTelemetrySetting to the Save button's #submit. When the triggering button defines its own #submit, Form API runs only those handlers and skips the form-level ones, so SiteInformationForm::submitForm() never ran and system.site was never written. The handler is now added to the form-level #submit ($form['#submit'][] = [$this, 'saveTelemetrySetting'];), so it runs after the form's own submit handler. The issue notes the bug is hidden when the form is submitted programmatically without the button as the triggering element, which is likely why existing tests missed it. The issue lists a functional test that saves the form through the UI as a remaining task. I did not see one in the repo and could not confirm it was added. No diff was available to me, so the fix is verified only against the current file, which shows the form-level line.

Upgrade

Update drupal_cms_helper to a release containing the fix. Any site information changes made through the form on affected versions were not saved and need to be re-entered.

item.title: #3591496: Drupal CMS 2.2.4 : Read-only installs have no site templates and the template step crashes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591496 · 1 contributor · 1 comment

Summary

In Drupal CMS 2.2.4, new projects ship without any site templates on disk. If the code directory is read-only (for example Pantheon in Git mode), the installer can only list templates already downloaded, so the "Choose a site template" step was empty and clicking Next threw a TypeError. The step now shows the error "There are no site templates available." and no longer offers a form that crashes. Note this only prevents the crash: such an install still cannot proceed without a template, so the first install needs a writable code directory.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

SiteTemplateForm::buildForm() in drupal_cms_installer merges SiteTemplate::findAll() with the curated online list. If the merged $all_choices is empty, it now adds a messenger error and returns the form early, before the template options and the actions element are built. That removes the Next button, and so the path where getChoice() returned null and caused the TypeError. The $form['#title'] assignment moved to the top so the title still shows on the early return. In drupal_cms_installer_theme.theme, the add_ons wrapper prefix and suffix are now set directly rather than with +=. The issue body's proposed test for the empty case is not part of the commit.
